answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a atlas as the anchor of the cost.
